title: Hazel and the Visitor
premise: Pest controller Lena Whitlock is called to the abandoned Harrow House, where she finds handprints too large to be human and hears a voice answering questions no one asked aloud. Digging into the town's founding families, she learns they bound something beneath the house with a ritual that requires a living descendant to renew it every fifty years—and this year's renewal was skipped. As the entity feeds on the town's sleepers, Lena discovers her own bloodline ties her to the founders, making her both the key and the sacrifice. In the end, she completes the ritual but cheats the price by binding the entity to herself instead of dying, becoming its new warden—alive, but never again alone in her own head.
about_author: Xanthe Lockridge is the pen name of a former rural building inspector who spent years documenting the strange things people leave behind in empty houses. They write horror rooted in blue-collar work, small-town secrets, and the conviction that old buildings remember.

chapters.title: The Call-Out
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A routine pest complaint at derelict Harrow House turns strange: droppings that aren't droppings, and handprints pressed into dust from the inside of a sealed wall. Lena rationalizes everything, as she always does. Emotional beat: professional calm masking a decade-old unease about things without explanations.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She photographs the prints—five fingers, but seven inches long, with whorls like tree rings. Her client, elderly Mabel Voss, begs her to leave before dark and mentions 'the answering.' Emotional beat: curiosity overriding instinct; the first crack in Lena's practiced skepticism.

chapters.title: The Noises Have Explanations
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present-day POV. Ten years ago, Lena's brother Dale vanished after a night job at Harrow House; police ruled it a runaway. She has built her whole life on explainable noises since. Emotional beat: grief fossilized into denial.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She leaves a recorder running overnight in the house to log 'animal activity.' Playback reveals a second voice—dry, patient—answering questions she never asked aloud, including one about Dale. Emotional beat: terror fused with terrible hope.

chapters.title: Mabel's Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Lena and Mabel. Mabel confesses her family were town founders and warns that the thing under Harrow House trades answers for access. It already knows Lena's name. Emotional beat: the horror of being expected.

chapters.title: Questions in the Dark
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Against judgment, she returns and asks the voice about Dale. It answers in Dale's own cadence, offering truth if she opens the cellar door. Emotional beat: loyalty to her brother warring with self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with archive interludes. In the county library she finds the 1874 founders' ledger: five families, a binding ritual, and a clause requiring renewal by bloodline every fifty years. The last signature is dated 1974—and unsigned. Emotional beat: dread of inherited obligation.

chapters.title: Sleepers
chapters.summary: Town-wide POV mosaic. Residents begin reporting identical nightmares of a doorway and waking with dirt under their nails. One man doesn't wake. Emotional beat: a community's slow suffocation, invisible to itself.

chapters.title: Bloodline
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A genealogist confirms it: Whitlock is an anglicized branch of the Wetherell founder line. Dale didn't run—he was taken as the unpaid price of a lapsed ritual. Emotional beat: rage at ancestors, guilt over ten years of believing the easy lie.

chapters.title: The Sheriff Who Knew
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Lena and Sheriff Ansel Boone, grandson of another founder. He admits the town has always known and paid quietly; he wants Lena gone before the equinox. Emotional beat: justice outside the law—the law itself is complicit.

chapters.title: What the Voice Wants
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The entity clarifies terms: complete the ritual, give a Wetherell life, and it sleeps another fifty years—or refuse, and it takes the whole town slowly. It shows her Dale, alive in some sense, kept as collateral. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Ansel's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sheriff Boone's POV. Boone offers himself instead—a founder's blood for the ritual—if Lena leaves town forever. But his hands shake; he's already been dreaming. Emotional beat: cowardice and courage indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Ritual, Described
chapters.summary: Lena's POV with ledger excerpts. She deciphers the full rite: salt lines cut with a founder's blood, names spoken backward, and the door opened from inside. The last step is unwritten—deliberately. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of understanding exactly what's required.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The town sleeps deeper than ever; three more don't wake. Mabel dies peacefully, whispering an apology to Lena. Emotional beat: mourning braided with resolve; the clock runs out at dawn.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She enters the cellar with salt, knife, and the ledger. The stairs go down farther than the house has depth. Boone follows, uninvited, insisting on his bargain. Emotional beat: claustrophobic courage.

chapters.title: Dale
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She finds Dale—not alive, not dead, a memory the entity wears like a coat. It offers him back permanently in exchange for her walking away. Emotional beat: the cruelest choice, love weaponized.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She refuses the counterfeit Dale and begins the rite. Boone tries to substitute himself and the entity rejects him—his fear has already fed it too much. Emotional beat: grief accepted, not escaped; loyalty finally pointed at truth.

chapters.title: Climax: The Unwritten Step
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the final line, Lena understands the omitted step: the ritual needs a willing vessel, not a corpse. She speaks her own name backward and binds the entity into herself rather than giving it her death. Emotional beat: defiant self-sacrifice that rewrites the rules.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Boone's POV. The town wakes; the nightmares stop. Boone covers the cellar with concrete and falsifies the record—one last act of justice outside the law, this time merciful. Emotional beat: exhausted, complicit relief.

chapters.title: Two Voices
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Back home, Lena catches herself answering questions aloud that no one asked. The entity is quiet, cooperative, and permanent. She starts recording again—for different reasons now. Emotional beat: uneasy coexistence; survival's price made daily.

chapters.title: What Lena Knows
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She visits Dale's empty grave and tells him the truth she couldn't tell for ten years. The voice inside her listens without mocking, and for the first time the noises have an explanation she can live with. Emotional beat: reconciliation with grief and with herself.

chapters.title: Renewal
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Lena's POV, years later. A young woman with Voss features knocks on Lena's door asking about noises in her walls. Lena recognizes the beginning of the next cycle—and takes the call. Emotional beat: the warden's burden passed forward, vigilance as inheritance.
